If they were capable people they would have built a rail  road system decades ago, but sub-Saharan Africans aren't even capable of maintaining the infrastructure left to them by the Europeans.

Many Southeast Asian countries were also colonized, and today those countries are either more prosperous than most European countries, or on an economic trajectory to surpass them by the end of this decade. So if colonialism has such long lasting negative repercussions, that it's still the cause of sub-Saharan Africa's inability to economically prosper, why does this phenomenon only seem to hinder sub-Saharan African countries?

I'll tell you why, it's because blaming Africa's problems on colonialism is bullsh*t. Africa's problems today are a direct result of the people who live there.
